item.title: Flydubai’s Tel Aviv flights to resume within weeks, 2 months after hijack bid
item.description: Flydubai has received approval from Israeli transportation minister Miri Regev to resume its flights to Tel Aviv. The approval came after a meeting where security arrangements were discussed to ensure safe operations. The airline previously suspended services after an incident involving an attempted hijacking by an Omani co-pilot. Services are expected to restart pending clearance from Israel's security establishment in the coming weeks.

item.title: Nuclear weapon in space? Russia may launch warhead-capable satellite by December
item.description: Russia is reportedly preparing to launch a satellite designed to carry a nuclear warhead by December. German intelligence has indicated that the satellite, known as Sputnik-S, has been assembled and stored for years. Dmitry Medvedev cites international law to justify potential nuclear weapon use, asserting state survival rights. He argues that international law permits nuclear usage in dire circumstances that threaten national existence.
item.dc:creator: Pranjal Pandey

item.title: Ohio golf-cart firms revive tax challenge over $37,500 in 2024 licence fees
item.description: In a significant legal battle, two golf-cart rental companies in Ohio took on the Village of Put-in-Bay, disputing what they deemed excessive tax fees imposed on their operations. They contended that these taxes were outside the village's jurisdiction. The Ohio Sixth District Court of Appeals has allowed portions of the challenge to move forward, although refund claims for a certain tax year were dismissed on procedural grounds.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Russia claims strikes on Starlink terminals, drone sites in Ukraine's Sumy
item.description: Russia's military conducted attacks on military sites in Ukraine's Sumy region using drones and missile strikes. In a separate incident, an overnight attack in Zaporizhzhia resulted in injuries to 11 individuals, including severe cases. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy issued warnings about impending Russian strike preparations while urging increased military aid from allies. He emphasized the importance of anti-ballistic missile systems for Ukraine's defense against aggression.
item.dc:creator: Pranjal Pandey

item.title: Sheikh Hasina requests Dec 16 return, picks Bangladesh Victory Day for comeback
item.description: Sheikh Hasina has announced her intention to return to Bangladesh on December 16, despite government threats. The current government has warned Hasina will face arrest upon her arrival for her past convictions. Following unrest and a student-led uprising, Hasina fled to India in August 2024, seeking asylum. Bangladesh's government has consistently reiterated its extradition request to India regarding Hasina.
item.dc:creator: Prisha Patnaik

item.title: ‘Unprovoked attack’: 2 Americans jailed for life for killing Canadian tech entrepreneur, partner
item.description: Two American men have been jailed for life in Dominica for the 2023 murder of Canadian tech entrepreneur Daniel Langlois and his partner, Dominique Marchand. A court sentenced Jonathan Lehrer and Robert Snyder Jr to two consecutive life terms each, describing the killings as an "unprovoked attack". The murders reportedly followed a long-running dispute over a road leading to Langlois' eco-resort.

item.title: ‘Justice is not for sale’: Newsom demands federal reforms to limit presidential pardon powers
item.description: California Governor Gavin Newsom has accused US President Donald Trump of turning presidential pardons into a business, alleging that wealthy allies and politically connected individuals have benefited from clemency. He called for sweeping federal reforms to limit presidential pardon powers. His remarks came after Trump criticised Newsom for granting clemency to 548 inmates on California's former death row.
item.dc:creator: Abhishek Mishra

item.title: US probes Iran, Russia link after 50 vessels face cyberattack: Report
item.description: Washington is investigating Iran's potential involvement in numerous cyberattacks against energy tankers carrying hazardous materials. This probe includes incidents where vessels received bomb threats alleging possible explosions. The investigation comes amid concerns that the conflict may expand beyond the Middle East into cyber operations. Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps reported three tankers caught fire after hitting naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: Dutch transgender activist Jason Bhugwandass dies by euthanasia at 28 after years of health struggles
item.description: Dutch transgender activist Jason Bhugwandass has died by euthanasia at 28 after years of physical and mental health struggles. Prime Minister Rob Jetten and Amsterdam mayor Femke Halsema paid tribute to him, remembering his fight against abuses in youth care institutions. His death was announced days after he fulfilled a final wish with a beach photoshoot alongside loved ones.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Lacy's Review: Lacy rates GTA 6 gameplay 10/10; story gets 6.5/10
item.description: Twitch streamer Nick "Lacy" rated GTA 6's gameplay a perfect 10/10 but gave its story just 6.5/10 after completing the game. He criticised the slow opening, saying the narrative improved around the 65-70% mark. Lacy also questioned the low payouts from major heists. Despite these complaints, he enjoyed the experience and revealed GTA 6 was the first story-mode game he had completed.
item.dc:creator: Global Sports Desk

item.title: 'Going to be a better CEO second time around': Jensen Huang returns to Nvidia HQ amid applause and cheers; watch
item.description: Jensen Huang returned to Nvidia as CEO after an independent investigation into his alleged extramarital affairs. His reinstatement followed a unanimous decision from Nvidia's board, satisfied with his transparency regarding the issues. Notably, Nvidia's stock surged dramatically, increasing by over 31% in a single day. Meanwhile, the Senate Banking Committee has scheduled a hearing for Huang on December 3.
